content.thinking:
I'm designing a towering 2.8m lava golem with cel-shaded basalt plates, glowing molten seams, and gold filigree accents in a Genshin-inspired style, planning to use robust geometry functions like joint, chain, sweep, and extrude while avoiding risky API calls.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton in rest pose: hips root, spine chain built from a catmull path through three points up to the chest, then a neck chain leading to an explicit head joint and jaw joint, all defined with world coordinates to avoid local-space ambiguity. I'm also planning how parts attach to specific bones using explicit "at" positions.

For the golem's proportions, I'm roughly 2.8m tall with stubby thick legs, a massive torso, and long arms reaching to the knees, laying out hip, knee, and ankle coordinates for each leg as a three-point path chain with a foot box part at the base.

I'm sweeping the leg bones with tapering radii using a faceted six-sided cross-section for a low-poly rounded look, then parenting the leg chains to the hips joint. For the torso I'm lofting a wide sweep along the spine chain with its own radius profile.

Now I'm laying out the pelvis, belly, and arm chain positions—shoulders, elbows, wrists with their x/y/z offsets—then planning the hand as a fist block with knuckle details for extra bulk.

Adding finger chains and joint hierarchy...

Now I'm designing the shoulder pauldrons as layered basalt plates using stacked spheres and boxes with flat shading, then moving to the head: a chunky sunken helm with glowing emissive eyes and a molten mouth slit positioned between the shoulders.

For the eyes, I'm working out whether to use glowing textured planes or simple emissive spheres, considering how the curvature of the head geometry affects where the eye surface sits—leaning toward a faceted block head shape instead of a smooth sphere so flat eye planes sit correctly on the surface.

I'll attach flame cards as frames on the head bone so they glow with their own colored texture, plus scatter small floating pyro embers near the arms and head for that Genshin pyro motif. For the mouth, I'm building a dark jaw box with a glowing interior tied to a jaw joint.

Working out exact head and jaw box coordinates...

For the neck chain, two points make one span, so I'll name it neck1 as the chain and neck2 as the tip. When passing a parent joint, I can pass a chain directly since it resolves to its tip joint — so the head parent should reference the neck chain's tip, and the neck chain's parent should be the spine chain's tip (chest). I'm setting up the spine chain with three points from hips through mid-torso to the top, naming each joint accordingly.

Now I'm sweeping the spine chain into the torso shape with a radius function, plus adding separate chest, belly, and back plates for extra detail. For the lava-seam texture, I'm thinking through how to render glowing cracks — using a cell-based paint function where seam borders get bright lava coloring, supplemented by separate glow-line sweeps since painted surfaces alone can't truly emit light.

Defining basalt stone paints...

I'll widen the seam to 0.1 for a bolder look, and work out texel density assuming ~25 m² of painted golem surface, landing around 6mm per texel with a 2048px paint size in a 4096 atlas for crispness. For the glowing seam gradient, I'm mapping distance thresholds to colors — yellow core near e<0.035, orange at <0.06, dark red-orange further out.

Beyond the lava seams, I want to add ornate gold detailing in a Genshin style: filigree bands at the wrists, a belt with a glowing Pyro emblem, gold-rimmed shoulder plates, and hanging red tassels, all set against the dark basalt to suggest an ancient seal-bound golem. I'm thinking the chest could feature a central glowing core ringed in gold with an SVG flame-glyph decal.

For the core itself, I'm working out placement using a glowing sphere plus a flat torus ring, trying to calculate where the torso's front surface actually sits in 3D space so the core embeds correctly rather than floating. Since the geometry math is uncertain, I'm considering using a raycast against the torso surface to find the actual hit point and placing the core there instead of guessing coordinates.

Now I'm designing the flame SVG texture with orange outer and yellow inner gradients, then figuring out how to arrange flame-shaped cards around the head like a crown using a ring layout with varied flow and lean, and starting to think about similar flame placements on the shoulders tied to the chest bone.

I also need to work out foot contact with the floor, keeping sink minimal by centering foot boxes near y=0.1 and letting the leg sweep's rounded cap meet the top, while adding small toe blocks for shape detail near the ankle bone.

Overall height checks out: head top around 2.53 with flames reaching toward 3.0 and horns near 2.8, giving the lava golem its towering basalt presence over a human figure, with flame cards adding a bit more at the crown. Now I'm positioning the arms—shoulders, elbows, wrists with specific coordinates—and varying the limb radius along its length so the forearm bulks out like a boulder.

Working out fist and finger placement...

Defining the leg chain positions for hip, knee, and ankle, naming them with side suffixes and parenting to the hips joint, then starting to sketch the pelvis geometry with a hip box and belt detail.

For the belt, I'm thinking through options like a swept torus versus an octagonal ring of gold plates placed around the waist ellipse, positioning each plate with trigonometric angles and rotating them to follow the torso's curve at the waistline.

Placing belly plates using surface raycasts to position stacked ab-like boxes against the torso contour, then adding angled pectoral slabs near the chest with slight tilt and rotation to suggest armor plating.

For the back, I'm planning a spine ridge of dark obsidian spikes positioned via rearward raycasts, plus layered dome pauldrons at the shoulders with scaled spheres and gold rim torii.

For rigging, I'm attaching the pauldrons to the chest spine tip so they stay fixed while the arms swing freely beneath, using the shoulder joint as the arm's first pivot. Upper arm armor plates then attach to that bone segment, positioned at the midpoint of the upper arm with proper aim orientation.

Switching to frustum boxes for flat-ended tapered plates instead of standard aimed geometry—these work better for gauntlets and forearm armor since width runs along world x and height follows the surface normal. I'm thinning the arm tube core and making it glow lava-colored, so molten light shows through the joints beneath the armor plates.

Same approach applies to legs and torso: a thin lava-glow core sweep with basalt block plates layered on top, leaving visible gaps at knees and shoulders. I'm setting up a `stone` helper function that wraps box geometry with flat-shaded cel paint, confirming the paint logic keys off vertex positions so it works regardless of the geometry's UV mapping.

I'm also planning a `slab` helper for creating basalt plate blocks with position, size, rotation, and bone attachment, plus thinking about using hexagonal cylinder prisms as basalt columns for a signature "organ pipe" look on shoulders, back, and lower legs, tilted via a direction vector.

Now I'm sketching the color palette—basalt lightness variants and a stone paint style with lava seams between cells, defining a molten crack function that maps distance between adjacent cell centers to a gradient of lava colors from pale yellow to deep red-black, with variations for seamed, sparsely-seamed, and plain stone surfaces.

Adding a darker basalt variant and a gold cel-shaded paint for accent parts, keeping the overall flat color count low.

Writing eye texture mirroring logic...

Now I'm positioning the eyes below a heavy brow ridge on the head, sizing them around 0.13x0.065 at roughly (±0.1, 2.42, 0.345), with the brow slab placed just above so the eyes sit recessed beneath it. I'm also planning small snout and cheek tusk details to add to the jaw.

Designing horn geometry...

I'm adding a crown of flames between the horns, plus floating pyro orbs as small glowing octahedrons around the chest area, echoing a Genshin vision motif. For the chest ornament I'm building a glowing core sphere with an inner brighter sphere, surrounded by a gold torus ring and four gold diamond-shaped cone spikes.

Then I'm considering a filigree texture plane for decoration — a spiral swirl pattern with flame motifs in gold on a dark plate, placed as a decal on the curved torso surface near the chest, positioned carefully so it doesn't get buried in the curved geometry.

I'm leaving pec plates offset to the sides so there's a free center strip for the decal, and skipping an extra belt buckle sigil. I'm also planning gold cord tassels with red ends hanging from the front of the belt.

I'm adding more tassels at the belt sides and pauldrons using a simple red-strand SVG shape, skipping the loincloth idea, and defining the thigh as a tapered stone block rigged to the hip bone from hip to knee.

Now I'm leaving a visible lava gap between the thigh and shin blocks at the knee, adding a hex-column stone knee cap, tapering the shin block from knee to ankle with a slight widening toward the foot, and checking the hip-to-knee tilt direction for the leg rig.

I'm defining a helper to build tapered segments along a line using lerp between two points, plus deciding whether to add armor plates layered on top of the thigh.

For the forearms, I'm bundling 5 hexagonal basalt columns of varying lengths around the lava core, each cylinder aimed along the arm's direction with slight radial offsets so they resemble organ pipes.

I'm also adding a blocky fist with small hex studs as knuckle spikes, plus gold cuffs at the wrist, elbow, and shoulder using tapered cylinders aligned to the forearm's axis, and setting up bone joints for the shoulder and elbow.

Setting up imports and bone structure...

I'll decide rng seeds for scattering embers, set up the meta export with name, style, and commit info, then start defining the color palette and builder function for the lava golem.

Building the skeleton now, setting up hips and a spine chain with catmull-rom points, and working out how to reference the chest tip joint safely by indexing into the chain's joints array.

Extending the skeleton upward with a neck chain parented to chest, then starting the head joint as a child of the neck.

Still shaping the torso sweep...

Adding chest pec plates for each side with outward-facing rotation and stone coloring, plus gold trim boxes along the pec bottoms for seam detailing.

Now I'm laying out abdominal plates in two rows, assigning the lower row to the spine1 bone and the upper row to spine2 so they follow the torso's natural bend zones.

Pectoral plates and pauldrons attach to spine2/chest tip, with the chest tip region having no child joint so parts stay rigid there. Arms are parented to the chest tip and move together without separate weighting.

For the back, I'm placing five spikes along a ridge curve from y=1.4 to 2.0, computing their base positions from the back silhouette function.

Now I'm adding obsidian spikes with varying length and radius, plus tilted basalt hex columns clustered behind the shoulders pointing up and back, and scattering flame card decals across the upper back surface using a filtered hit-scatter with lean and flow parameters for a fiery visual effect.

Adding shoulder pauldron flames, head crown flames in a circular arrangement...

Writing flame texture SVG...

Adjusting the flame path shape...

I'm sketching the eyelid shapes with slanted upper edges, layering an orange outer shape, a yellow highlight, and a pale ellipse for the eye itself, angled so the slant points toward the nose.

Writing mirrored eye function...

Adding a vertical glowing vein down the gap between ab plates...

Widening plate spacing so the vein stays visible, then placing the core sphere and a ring torus around it. Now I'm starting the arm-generation loop, iterating over left/right sides to build symmetric limbs...

Still writing arm chain logic...

Positioning gauntlet columns around the forearm...

Adding knuckle studs and finger joint chain coordinates...

Still positioning limb joints...

Adding shoulder tassels now, double-checking pauldron height clears the head, then setting up the leg chains from hip to knee to ankle joints.

Now I'm defining the thigh and knee geometry, placing a dodecahedron knee guard with a flat secondary stone material, then starting the shin block segment.

Continuing to shin, foot, and toe placement...

Still placing belt plates and buckle...

I'm positioning abs rows and checking pec overlap, then setting vein points down the core toward the belt buckle, and starting to lay out the head parts like the skull box relative to the head joint.

Now I'm sketching the head geometry: a top slab, brow, cheeks, nose, eye planes, and a jaw with a slight gap for a glowing mouth slab, placing teeth cones from the head bottom.

Attaching tusks to the jaw sides with angled spikes, then adding gold ear discs as cylindrical accents, and planning to paint lava crack details onto the head using the stone material.

Next I'm adding a crest of cylindrical columns at the back of the skull for a flame-crown effect, then scattering floating ember octahedrons around the body using randomized but deterministic positions that stay clear of the torso radius.

Writing tassel SVG...

Writing SVG filigree code...

For the back view I'll add lava cracks, spine ridge spikes, hex columns, and embers. Tallying up the part counts across torso, hips, pauldrons, arms, legs, and head, I'm estimating roughly 200 total pieces for the whole figure.

I should also add rivets on the pauldron rims, belt buckle, and cuffs as small decorative spheres, bumping the count up by maybe 36 parts, which stays comfortably under budget. Now I'm setting up a helper function for creating boxes positioned on bones with color and rotation...

Figuring out the right types to import -- Joint from skeleton, Fill/Paint from the paint module -- so the helper signatures stay consistent with the rest of the build.

Now I'm working out the cylinder helper: using CylinderGeometry oriented so the top radius points toward the limb's tip, computing direction vectors between joints with Vector3 subtraction and normalization, and feeding those points into the chain path builder.

I'm also sketching helper functions for frustum boxes between two points with varying widths/heights, wrapping sweeps and card flames in glow effects, and setting up surface scatter on the torso filtered by normal direction to decide where decals or cards attach.

Now I'm defining the torso's stone material with eight sides and flat shading, sweeping the spine chain with rounded caps, and building the neck as a smaller cylinder connecting up to the head, then placing small white plane geometries for the eyes.

I'm checking that the brow box sits properly above the eyes without overlapping, and verifying the head box dimensions leave room for the brow to glow slightly at its top edge. Now I'm setting up horn sweeps using catmull-rom curves with varying radius along the path.

Flame effects on the horn tips need a bone attachment for positioning, and I'm sketching out hex-shaped column placements along the golem's back, looping through positions with alternating heights and lengths to create a staggered armor pattern.

Now I'm defining the back spikes as a function that places cylindrical shapes anchored to the spine joints, varying their vertical positions and directions to fan outward from the torso.

I'm setting up a helper that casts a ray against the torso surface to find where points sit along the back, which I'll use for positioning features like spikes and belt plates once the torso mesh exists. I'm also noting gold paint for the belt plates and double-checking that paint types and imports like `frame` and `lerp` are properly used.

Now I'm writing a `molten` paint function that uses cell noise to create a lava-like gradient—white-hot core fading through yellow, orange, and dark red into the base color based on distance from cell edges. I'm considering adding a vertical heat gradient so the lower body appears hotter than the upper body.

I also want to verify the `cel` wrapper correctly resolves nested Paint shadows through `shadowOf` and `resolve`, and how baked UV paints interact with box geometry.

Setting up the builder function and random seed, then defining a vector helper to start constructing the lava golem's geometry piece by piece.

Adding column and sphere helpers...

Now I'm checking the Joint type imported from the skeleton module, confirming that joints returned by b.joint and chain.joints are properly typed, then writing symmetric arm chains for left and right sides with shoulder, elbow, and wrist points parented to the chest.

Verifying the polyline path logic -- with three named joints spanning two segments plus the tip, destructuring arm.joints into upper, fore, and hand. Building glowing frustum segments swept along each arm's path with tapered radii and rounded caps hidden at the fists.

Now I'm aligning the upper arm's frustum box axis to the actual bone direction, checking how the pauldron covers the top. Making sure there's a visible lava gap near the elbow between the upper block end and forearm column start, roughly 0.2 meters with a glowing core showing through, and adding thin gold rim rings at the block ends to mark the elbow joint.

Working through the forearm columns, wrist cuff placement, and fist box positioning so everything connects smoothly at the wrist without gaps. Then I'm setting up the finger sweeps as chained bones with tapered polygon cross-sections in a secondary stone color, adding small glowing sphere tips at each fingertip joint, and mirroring the same approach for the thumb.

Now I'm defining the legs: foot boxes positioned at the ankle joints with proper spacing for toes, shin blocks connecting knee to ankle, dodecahedron knee guards with small spikes, gold anklets wrapped around the lower leg, and hip tassets as simple boxes—then moving on to the eye texture function and other remaining details.

I'm now compositing the final answer, double-checking TypeScript strictness for unused variables, and generating a loop that spawns small glowing ember octahedrons near the chest with randomized positions, colors, and sizes—adjusting the x-offset so they don't overlap the arm geometry.

I'm positioning tassel frames around the belt and pauldrons using angle-based placements, and updating the eye SVG so the pupil slit uses the dark ink color for contrast against the glow effect. I'm also confirming the decal options for position and direction are correctly formatted.

Checking band color arrays and rotation tuples for type correctness, then finishing up the torso skin definition before writing the file.
